svg.title: Who does what when people connect and sign in
svg.desc: Four separate jobs. An administrator configures token verification with WEAVE_OIDC_PROVIDERS, publishes public sign-in settings and allowed flows with WEAVE_CLIENT_SIGN_IN, registers a public login client with PKCE and loopback callbacks at the identity provider, and links each person and grants access. Each person enters the server address, reviews the identity provider once, signs in at the provider in a browser or with a code, and picks an authorized workspace. Local pairing only connects Studio's page to the Studio host on the same computer and grants nothing on the platform. The platform checks grants on every request; hiding a button in Studio is only a convenience.
svg.text: Who does what when people connect
An administrator prepares the platform once. Each person then connects and signs in.
Administrator · once per platform
Local development: weave platform setup does steps 1–3 with its own Keycloak; weave platform user, step 4.
Configure token verification
WEAVE_OIDC_PROVIDERS: issuer, signing keys (JWKS), audience, and which client IDs sign in people.
Publish the sign-in settings
WEAVE_CLIENT_SIGN_IN: the login client, scopes, and allowed flows (browser, device). No secrets.
Register the login client at your identity provider
A public client with PKCE S256, plus the device code grant if people may sign in with a code.
Callbacks http://127.0.0.1/callback and http://[::1]/callback, accepting any loopback port.
Link each person and grant access
Link provider, issuer, and subject to a principal; grant roles in a tenant, project, or environment.
Studio and the CLI read these settings from GET /api/v1/client-configuration: public, no secrets.
Your grants decide which workspaces appear in step 4 below.
Person · on each computer
In Studio, choose Connect to a platform. In a terminal, run weave auth setup SERVER.
Enter the server address
For example weave.example.com. HTTPS is required except on this computer (loopback).
Review the identity provider once
The saved platform pins the issuer and login client; changing them needs a new review.
Sign in at your identity provider
In a browser on this computer, or with a code on another device. Weave never sees your password.
Pick an authorized workspace
You see only the tenants, projects, and environments your grants allow.
Local pairing is not sign-in
Studio’s page pairs with the Studio host
on this computer (127.0.0.1 only). In a
browser, type the one-time terminal code.
Pairing grants nothing on the platform.
The platform decides access
Server-side grants check every request
in its tenant, project, and environment.
Provider role claims do not grant access.
Hidden buttons in Studio are only a convenience.

g.text: Sign-in proves who you are. Only the platform’s grants decide what you may do.
